newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk party says backs army demands on Islamists.
newsitem.headline: Turk party says backs army demands on Islamists.

text.p: Turkey's junior coalition party said on Monday it would work to persuade the Islamist wing of the government to put into force anti-Islamist measures demanded by the secularist military.

"The necessary work will be done at the next cabinet meeting to carry out these recommendations," conservative True Path Party (DYP) deputy chairman Cihan Pacaci told Reuters. "Coalition is the art of compromise," he said.
Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan last week reluctantly signed a directive from the military demanding a crackdown on Islamist militancy.

But it is unclear whether Erbakan will move against Islamist activists, his core constituents, in practice. The cabinet is due to discuss the military demands, inlcuding enforcing bans on Islamist dress, at a weekly meeting on Thursday.
Erbakan became modern Turkey's first Islamist leader last June in a coalition agreement with pro-Western Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller's DYP.
